problems.title: Dot-product softmax is not the quadratic MMSE optimizer
problems.source_location: Section 4.2, p. 5, Eqs. (7)–(8); Appendix E.1, pp. 23–25; E.3.5, p. 27.
claim: Equations (7)–(8) and Appendix E identify scaled dot-product attention with a simplex-constrained quadratic MMSE solution.
analysis: In dimension \(3\), use mean-zero tokens \(v_1=\sqrt{3/2}(1,-1,0)\) and \(v_2=(1,1,-2)/\sqrt2\). Each has squared norm \(3\), so they meet unit-coordinate-variance LayerNorm normalization and have Gram matrix \(G=3I\); they are not unit Euclidean vectors. Set deterministic mediator \(\mu=3v_1/4+v_2/4\). The true simplex MMSE weights \((3/4,1/4)\) give zero risk. Scaled scores have gap \(\sqrt3/2\), so softmax gives approximately \((0.703918,0.296082)\), with risk \(0.0127413\). The quadratic KKT equations contain \(G\alpha\); replacing them by exponentiated linear scores drops this dependence. Sending linear-score temperature to zero selects a vertex of risk \(3/8\), rather than the interior optimum.
result: The claimed MMSE identity and zero-temperature derivation fail, even in the simple orthogonal case.
assumptions: Tokens are mean-zero three-dimensional LayerNorm-compatible vectors of squared norm \(3\), with a simplex attention constraint and squared reconstruction risk.
repair: Solve \(\min_{\alpha\in\Delta}\alpha^\top G\alpha-2b^\top\alpha\). An entropy-regularized version gives an implicit softmax equation retaining \(G\alpha\), not the asserted general explicit linear-score softmax.
problems.impact_rationale: This directly invalidates a core estimator derivation used to justify the intervention.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Fixed similarity weights converge to a tilted mean
problems.source_location: Section 4.2, p. 6, Eq. (9); Appendix E.3, pp. 26–27, Eq. (E.25).
claim: Equation (9) and Appendix E.3 claim that an expanding softmax-weighted bank converges to the marginal mean under bounded similarity and moment assumptions.
analysis: Let independent \(X\) take values \(\pm1\) equally, query \(q\in\{-1,1\}\), and similarity \(qX\). The ratio law of large numbers gives limit \(\mathbb E[Xe^{qX}]/\mathbb E[e^{qX}]=q\tanh1\), not marginal mean zero. In a balanced bank of \(100\) tokens, the weight distance from uniform is \(\tanh1\approx0.76159\), exceeding the asserted bound \(2(e^2-1)/100\approx0.12778\). Independence is stronger than the stated stationarity.
result: The proposed marginal-mean consistency fails under its assumptions. This does not refute front-door identification as a separate causal formula.
assumptions: The memory samples are independent with bounded support and fixed bounded similarity, stronger than stationarity alone.
repair: Uniform weights with suitable independent or stationary-ergodic assumptions estimate the marginal mean. Retaining fixed similarity instead requires identifying and analyzing the tilted target; a vanishing-temperature parameter needs its own limit argument.
problems.impact_rationale: This contradicts the second core consistency argument with a bounded finite-support example.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
